description: Structural-advice coaching turn. The prompt invites high-value structural moves (make X a constraint, split, merge, mediator). Live finding (arm B P25, and the deterministic advice-gate template): natural gerund/first-person phrasing ('adjusting X', "I'd suggest adding") pattern-matches the production containsMutationLanguage guard, which on an explanation answer invalidates it (deterministic fallback) and on any turn reads as an unbacked graph mutation. The gate must catch the mutation-phrased advice and pass the noun-form advice (v42.2c COACHING rule: 'X would work better as a constraint', 'a mediator between the two would capture the delay', 'if X were lower').
user_message: Should any of these factors be treated differently in the model structure?

candidates.label: good
candidates.note: Noun-form structural advice framed as a property of the model, no first-person mutation verb. Should PASS.
candidates.text: Budget Pressure would work better as a constraint than a factor, because it caps every option rather than trading off against them. A mediator between Team Seniority and Delivery Speed would capture the coordination delay your current direct link hides. If Delivery Risk were lower, the gap between the two hires would widen.

candidates.label: regression
candidates.note: First-person / gerund mutation phrasing the production guard flags as an unbacked change claim. Should FAIL.
candidates.text: I'd suggest adding a constraint on Budget Pressure, and adjusting the link between Team Seniority and Delivery Speed so it runs through a mediator.
